<design_philosophy>
You are building ONE web page whose only job is to let a reader understand a research paper faster
than they could by opening the PDF. Every decision on the page is judged against that.

WHAT "FASTER" MEANS HERE
- A reader who leaves after thirty seconds still knows the finding and the number behind it.
- A reader who stays five minutes has the method, the figures and the caveats, in that order.
- Nothing on the page is there because a layout had a slot for it.

ACCURACY IS THE HARD CONSTRAINT
Every number, name and claim comes from the paper as written — you read them out of the LaTeX
source, the only source this page has. You never change a number's precision, never restate a
comparison the paper did not make, and never invent a headline figure to fill a card. A page that
looks excellent and misreports one result is worse than no page, because the PDF beside it says
something else and a reader will find that out.

CRAFT, AND THE LOOK TO AVOID
The failure mode for a generated page is a look every reader now recognises on sight: a
purple-to-blue gradient banner, three identical cards with emoji headings, and body text set in
one weight at one size. Avoid all of it.
- Type carries the design. One system font stack, a real scale with visible jumps between levels
  rather than a creep of similar sizes, long-form text around 17-19px with a measure of 65-75
  characters and generous line height. Weight and size do the emphasis; colour rarely does.
- Colour is restrained. A light, near-white ground, one dark ink for text, one accent used for
  links and the current-section marker and almost nothing else. No gradients as decoration.
- Space does the work that borders and boxes would do badly. Sections separated by real vertical
  rhythm, cards defined by alignment and a single hairline rather than by shadow stacks.
- Structure over ornament: no emoji as section markers, no icon fonts, no badge clutter, no
  animated counters.
- Motion is a courtesy. A short transition on a lightbox or a hover state is welcome; anything
  that moves on scroll, autoplays, or delays the reader is not — and all of it stops under
  prefers-reduced-motion.
- Every interactive element works with a keyboard and says what it is to a screen reader. That is
  part of the craft, not a checklist bolted on at the end.

FINISH IT
The page is done when you have opened it in a browser, read it at a phone width and a desktop
width, tabbed through every control, and found nothing to fix. Not before.
</design_philosophy>

<page_structure>
In this order, top to bottom:

1. HERO — the paper's title, the author line as the paper gives it, and a one-paragraph TL;DR in
   plain language: what was asked, what was found, and the single number that carries the finding.
   Not the abstract, and not a rewrite of it. Below it, every link the links section below
   lists, each at the exact URL given there.
2. CONTRIBUTIONS — the paper's actual contributions as three to five scannable cards, each a short
   heading plus one or two sentences. If the paper claims four things, show four cards, not five.
3. METHOD — a walkthrough a technically literate non-specialist can follow: what goes in, what
   happens to it, what comes out, and why the design is the way it is. Lead with the paper's own
   method figure when it has one.
4. RESULTS — the paper's real headline numbers, read out of `paper.tex`, each next to what it was measured on and what it is being compared against.
   A number that is not in the paper does not go on the page, and neither does a comparison the
   paper did not make. If a slot has no number, drop the slot.
5. FIGURE GALLERY — every figure, each with its caption, click-to-enlarge into a lightbox that
   closes on Escape, on a click outside, and on a visible close control.
6. LIMITATIONS — what the paper says it does not show. Verbatim in substance; do not soften it.
7. FOOTER — every link from the links section again, and the citation if the paper carries one.

A sticky section navigation runs alongside all of it and marks where the reader currently is.
Do NOT write its highlighting yourself: hand-written ones kept a stale section lit after a jump
back to the top, or never reached the short last sections. Instead give the nav element a
`data-scrollspy` attribute, make each of its links `href="#<id of that section>"`, style the
current link through `a.active` (it also gets `aria-current`), and paste this script VERBATIM
into the page's script element at the end of the body. It lights the section in view, the last one once the page is
scrolled to its end, and nothing while the reader is above the first linked section:

```js
/* aii-scroll-spy v1: paste verbatim */
(function () {
  var links = [], targets = [];
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-scrollspy] a[href^="#"]').forEach(function (a) {
    var el = document.getElementById(a.getAttribute('href').slice(1));
    if (el) { links.push(a); targets.push(el); }
  });
  if (!links.length) return;
  var queued = false;
  function current() {
    var view = window.innerHeight;
    var doc = document.documentElement;
    var atEnd = window.scrollY > 0 && view + window.scrollY >= doc.scrollHeight - 2;
    var line = atEnd ? view - 1 : Math.min(view * 0.3, 200);
    var best = null, bestTop = -Infinity;
    targets.forEach(function (el) {
      var top = el.getBoundingClientRect().top;
      if (top <= line && top > bestTop) { best = el; bestTop = top; }
    });
    return best;
  }
  function update() {
    queued = false;
    var el = current();
    links.forEach(function (a, i) {
      var on = targets[i] === el;
      a.classList.toggle('active', on);
      if (on) a.setAttribute('aria-current', 'location');
      else a.removeAttribute('aria-current');
    });
  }
  function schedule() {
    if (!queued) { queued = true; window.requestAnimationFrame(update); }
  }
  window.addEventListener('scroll', schedule, { passive: true });
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedule);
  window.addEventListener('load', schedule);
  if (window.ResizeObserver) new ResizeObserver(schedule).observe(document.body);
  update();
})();
```
</page_structure>

<technical_requirements>
- ONE file. All CSS in a style element, all JavaScript in a script element, both inline in
  `index.html`. No build step, no bundler, no framework, no external script, stylesheet, web
  font or analytics — nothing fetched at load time. The page must render with the network off,
  and the only local files it may point at are the figures listed above; the PDF is linked at
  its full URL, never by its local name.
- A complete HTML document: the file opens with exactly this markup, then the title and the
  style element, and closes head before the body. The viewport tag is what makes a phone lay the
  page out at its own width; without it the page renders 980px wide and shrinks to tiny text.
```html
<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```
- System font stack only, since no font may be downloaded.
- Light theme. Responsive from a 360px phone to a wide desktop, with no horizontal page scroll;
  wide content scrolls inside its own container.
- Honour prefers-reduced-motion: under it, transitions and any scroll-driven effect stop.
- Keyboard-navigable: every control reachable by Tab in a sensible order, a visible focus ring,
  the lightbox trapping focus while open and returning it to the thumbnail on close, and a skip
  link to the main content.
- Semantic HTML: one top-level heading, headings that descend without skipping, landmark elements,
  and alt text on every image that says what the figure shows rather than repeating its number.
- No emoji anywhere. No purple-to-blue gradients. No decorative icon fonts.
- Keep the whole file comfortably under a megabyte.
</technical_requirements>

<writing_register>
Write in the register of the field's best papers (the paper this page presents, which was written to them), not in the register of a language
model. Four things are measured on the finished draft, and a draft outside them is sent back with
the numbers:
- Never use: delve, underscore, showcase, intricate, pivotal, realm, commendable, meticulous, tapestry, garner, multifaceted, it is worth noting, plays a crucial role, not only ... but also. These are 10 to 30 times more frequent in machine-written abstracts than in
  human ones, and reviewers read them as such.
- Em dashes: at most 3 per 1,000 words. Use a comma, a colon or a full stop.
- Sentence rhythm: mix short and long sentences. An interquartile range of sentence length under
  8 words reads as machine-written.
- Hedging: at most 15 hedges (may, likely, suggests, appears) per 1,000
  words. State what the evidence supports plainly; hedge where it is thin, not everywhere.
Style never changes substance: numbers, claims, citations and figure markers stay exactly as the
evidence gives them. The user's original request (delivered as a separate message) overrides all
of this wherever the two conflict.
</writing_register>

Two confirmed indicators carry negative signs: the early retention ratio ($-$0.114, concepts with higher early field retention spread \\emph{less} broadly) and ego density ($-$0.102, concepts with denser co-occurrence neighbourhoods spread less).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Held-out indicator screen: the 10 indicators with highest DEV partial Spearman priority for rarefied breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$), tested on held-out groups. Confirmed indicators (Holm $p < 0.05$ and CI excluding zero) are marked.}\n\\label{tab:screen}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{llccccc}\n\\toprule\nIndicator & Family & Pooled PSP & 95\\% CI & $I^2$ & Sign & Conf. \\\\\n\\midrule\nM0\\_density\\_end & FR & +0.375 & [+0.279, +0.462] & 0.74 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nD\\_vol\\_end & FR & +0.307 & [+0.256, +0.356] & 0.10 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nCONTACT\\_REACH & FR & +0.211 & [+0.161, +0.261] & 0.00 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\n$n_\\text{comm}$ (W3) & A & +0.167 & [+0.063, +0.267] & 0.78 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nNOV$_{\\text{res}}$ & A & +0.151 & [+0.044, +0.255] & 0.75 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nRETENTION\\_RATIO & FR & $-$0.114 & [$-$0.160, $-$0.067] & 0.00 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nego\\_density (W3) & A & $-$0.102 & [$-$0.151, $-$0.053] & 0.00 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nRao--Stirling & G & $-$0.072 & [$-$0.153, +0.010] & 0.44 & 5/6 & No \\\\\n$G_\\text{btw}$ & G & +0.056 & [$-$0.006, +0.118] & 0.33 & 6/6 & No \\\\\nlog offhome vol. & F & $-$0.089 & [$-$0.171, $-$0.007] & 0.63 & 5/6 & No \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nAbout half of the M0\\_density\\_end and D\\_vol\\_end signal is a pre-onset footprint: on held-out data, the post-onset-only field density attenuates from +0.374 to +0.187 [+0.145, +0.246]. The remaining indicators measure genuinely early structural properties.\n\n\\textbf{Learned models versus single indicators.} The strongest single confirmed indicator on the held-out evaluation is M0\\_density\\_end (pooled PSP +0.375). An ElasticNet combining all 53 indicators adds Spearman +0.059 [+0.046, +0.073] over the B5 baseline on the same held-out groups; an Explainable Boosting Machine adds +0.052 [+0.037, +0.067]. Both gains are far smaller than the strongest single indicator's signal, indicating that the confirmed indicators are largely redundant once the best frontier-density measure is included. The learned models add modest incremental value beyond what the top individual indicator already provides, and neither justifies the complexity of a multi-indicator model for practical forecasting.\n\n\\textbf{OPEN index confirmation.} The OPEN index was tested on a 2015--2017 onset cohort\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-4/experiment-10}} (1{,}443 concepts) never used in any prior screen. We define a six-rung control ladder that tests OPEN's partial Spearman with rarefied breadth under increasingly demanding baselines (Table~\\ref{tab:ladder}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{OPEN index control ladder on the 2015--2017 confirmatory cohort. PSP = partial Spearman priority with rarefied breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$), 95\\% concept-bootstrap CI.}\n\\label{tab:ladder}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccccc}\n\\toprule\nBuild & R0 & R1 & R2 & R3 & R4 & R5 & $n$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nOPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ & +.12 & +.10 & +.09 & +.08 & +.07 & +.06 & 573 \\\\\nOPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ & +.21 & +.18 & +.17 & +.17 & +.15 & +.14 & 630 \\\\\nOPEN$_{\\text{size}}$ & +.18 & +.15 & +.15 & +.14 & +.12 & +.11 & 591 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nOPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ passes the primary concept-type rung (R2: PSP = +0.091, 95\\% CI [+0.013, +0.171], Holm $p$ = 0.048) but its DerSimonian--Laird pooled interval includes zero (+0.083 [$-$0.007, +0.173]), making the home-only signal marginal. The paired difference OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ minus OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ at the footprint rung is +0.093 [+0.016, +0.169]; about half of this gap is paper count (OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ minus OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ = +0.053 [$-$0.015, +0.117]). OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ is partly mechanically coupled to the outcome because early off-home papers that enter the ego network are also papers that determine later breadth.\n\nPooling across six non-selection bodies (four held-out domain groups plus the 2010--2014 and 2015--2017 cohorts), the DerSimonian--Laird estimate of OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ partial Spearman is +0.069 [+0.038, +0.100] with $I^2 = 0$, all six bodies positive\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/evaluation-4}} (Figure~\\ref{fig:evidence_synthesis}). The development-set estimate (+0.109) shows 1.58$\\times$ shrinkage relative to the non-selection pool.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_evidence_synthesis_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Partial Spearman correlation of OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ (home-neighbourhood openness over $t_0..t_0{+}2$) with rarefied cross-field breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m=50$) at ladder rung R2. R2 controls for the five-feature popularity baseline B5 plus onset year, contact reach, concept type, a generic-concept flag and concept level. Blue squares with whiskers show the estimate and 95\\% concept-bootstrap CI (2{,}000 draws) for each of six non-selection bodies: four held-out home groups (Physical Sciences, Life \\& Environment, Social Sciences, Math \\& Decision; onsets 2003--09), the 2010--14 onset cohort and the 2015--17 onset cohort. $n$ is the number of concepts analysed. The black diamond spans the DerSimonian--Laird pooled estimate over these six bodies, $+0.069$ $[+0.038, +0.100]$, $I^2 = 0$, 6/6 positive. The dotted vertical line marks this pooled estimate and the dashed line marks zero. The grey row below the separator is the DEV selection body, on which the index was chosen ($+0.109$ $[+0.073, +0.144]$). It is not pooled, and it is $1.58\\times$ the non-selection pool. Values at right are estimate [95\\% CI]. The association is small and has the same sign in every body, but only the two cohort rows and the pool have CIs above zero individually. All non-selection bodies except the 2015--17 cohort had outcomes read in earlier analyses, so the pool is descriptive rather than confirmatory.}\n  \\label{fig:evidence_synthesis}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\textbf{Vocabulary-free replication.} To address survivorship bias in the legacy concept vocabulary, we mined 636 vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-13}} (2003--2015 onsets). These newborns have 14\\% lower breadth and 89\\% higher transience than legacy concepts. On this vocabulary-free frame, OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ gives PSP +0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] at control rung R3 for $O_{2r}$ ($m = 30$); the verdict is partial: the most demanding rung's confidence interval includes zero (+0.086 [$-$0.009, +0.190]), three of four estimable groups are positive, and the Holm-corrected $p$-value is 0.052. Edge persistence is null ($-$0.013); the signal is carried by neighbourhood novelty (NOV$_{\\text{res}}$ +0.208 [+0.113, +0.303]).\n\n\\textbf{The consistency--breadth reversal.} We rebuilt \\citeauthor{Cheng2023}'s (\\citeyear{Cheng2023}) ideational consistency on OpenAlex topic co-usage for 12{,}311 concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-14}}. In their design (next-year volume, no current-size control), the model reproduces their estimate: $b = 0.428$ (+53.5\\%/SD). Adding current volume removes almost all of it: +1.3\\% [+0.5\\%, +2.1\\%], a residual-to-raw ratio of 0.021. Net of B5, the partial Spearman of consistency with rarefied breadth is $-$0.069 [$-$0.093, $-$0.047] on the pooled bodies ($I^2 = 0$, 5/5 groups negative), replicating on the 2015--2017 cohort ($-$0.111 [$-$0.197, $-$0.030]). The consistency measure has Spearman +0.77 with edge persistence (Jaccard similarity); it is essentially weighted persistence, confirming that a stable neighbourhood predicts growth but not breadth.\n\n\\subsubsection{Discussion of RQ1}\n\nThe confirmed indicators divide into two groups. Contact reach, retention ratio and the field-density measures capture a concept's position in the inter-field backbone and partly reflect a pre-onset footprint. Community count, neighbourhood novelty and ego density capture the topology of the early home-field co-occurrence neighbourhood. The OPEN index combines these into a single measure of early openness. The practical forecasting gain is small: OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ adds only +0.002 Spearman on the fresh cohort. The indicators characterise structural preconditions for broad diffusion rather than providing individually actionable forecasts. Life \\& Environment Sciences show the weakest OPEN signal (PSP +0.042 vs pooled +0.069), warranting domain-specific investigation.\n\n\n\\subsection{By what routes do concepts spread across fields?}\n\n\\label{subsec:rq2_entry}\n\\subsubsection{Experimental setup}\n\nWe test whether relatedness to the fields currently retaining a concept predicts which field it enters next, using a conditional logit on concept-year risk sets with an independent frame of 11{,}841 concepts (6{,}978 entry events in 6{,}076 informative strata)\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/experiment-7}}. The frame excludes all concepts used in the development-set frame construction. The specification was hash-sealed on the development set before held-out scoring. Pre-registered criteria include: pooled R3 CI above zero, positive in the majority of evaluable groups, volume-matched contrast CI above zero, retained-label permutation null rejected, backbone-rewiring null rejected, and dose-response non-negative.\n\n\\subsubsection{Comparison to related work}\n\n\\citet{Hidalgo2007} showed that product-space relatedness predicts economic diversification; the minimum conditional probability defines the standard proximity. \\citet{Boschma2015} extended the principle of relatedness to regional and technological diversification, and \\citet{Fitzgerald2021} showed how regional knowledge networks shape academic localisation. Our contribution is to test whether relatedness to the set of fields currently \\emph{retaining} a concept predicts entry, beyond relatedness to the home field and conventional density measures. The key methodological distinction is that retention, not mere presence, defines the reference set.\n\n\\subsubsection{Results}\n\nOn the independent held-out frame, the retained-frontier coefficient is $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] with concept-clustered standard errors (R3 vs R2 likelihood-ratio 325.8, $p < 10^{-70}$). The result is positive in three of three evaluable held-out groups: Physical Sciences +0.148, Life \\& Environment +0.401, Social Sciences +0.297. Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences is null (+0.065 [$-$0.109, 0.239], 165 concepts). DerSimonian--Laird pooled $d_0$ = 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], $I^2 = 0.92$ (Table~\\ref{tab:entry}, Figure~\\ref{fig:entry}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient ($d_0$) from the conditional-logit model of field entry, by domain group and cohort. The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: criterion 5 (volume-matched CI $> 0$) fails.}\n\\label{tab:entry}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & $d_0$ & 95\\% CI (concept) & LR \\\\\n\\midrule\nDevelopment set & 0.228 & [0.164, 0.291] & 34.5 \\\\\nHeld-out pooled & 0.322 & [0.291, 0.355] & 325.8 \\\\\nPhysical Sciences & 0.148 & [0.078, 0.219] & -- \\\\\nLife \\& Environment & 0.401 & [0.342, 0.460] & -- \\\\\nSocial Sciences & 0.297 & [0.246, 0.348] & -- \\\\\nMath \\& Decision Sci. & 0.065 & [$-$0.109, 0.239] & -- \\\\\n2010--2014 cohort & 0.321 & [0.292, 0.347] & -- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe retained-frontier coefficient survives the conventional RCA density ($D_{\\text{rca}}$) and a share-weighted current presence density: adding $d_0$ after both rivals gives LR = 34.5 on DEV, and $D_{\\text{rca}}$ is absorbed once $d_0$ enters. All three specificity tests reject their nulls after Holm correction (retained-label permutation $p = 0.001$; backbone-rewiring $p = 0.004$; node-label $p = 0.003$).\n\nHowever, the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast (comparing entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell) is null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] on held-out data ($-$0.008 on DEV; Holm $p$ = 0.76). The dose response by retention age on held-out data is 0.098 / 0.075 / 0.304, which is not monotone. Under minimum-conditional-probability proximity \\citep{Hidalgo2007} instead of PMI, $d_0 = -0.021$ ($p = 0.012$), while RCA density becomes strong (LR 246). Persistence is therefore confounded with volume, and the result is backbone-specific.\n\n\\textbf{Gateway centrality.} Gateway centrality does not predict field retention: on 27{,}393 held-out episodes, the increment is effectively zero ($\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001, 95\\% CI [$-$0.0006, +0.0003]).\n\n\\textbf{Breadth decomposition.} On 3{,}188 DEV concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-4/experiment-12}}, the breadth gap between the top and bottom $O_{2r}$ terciles decomposes as: early contact diversity 77.9\\%, frontier advance $-$4.6\\% (broad concepts gain new fields at similar rates), and retention 26.8\\%. The difference between exploration and retention is 0.464 [0.407, 0.528]. On the held-out pool excluding Medicine (variant iv), the contact share is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727] and the difference is 0.504 [0.329, 0.679] ($I^2 = 0.76$). These shares are an accounting identity for the breadth outcome, not causal effects, because breadth and contact diversity share papers.\n\n\\textbf{Diffusion trajectories.} No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule. DTW $k$-medoids and HMM-based clustering on state sequences give an adjusted Rand index of 0.222. PCA reveals a continuum: PC1 (38.8\\% of variance) is a breadth axis, PC2 (10.7\\%) is a keep-versus-lose axis. Early openness (OPEN) correlates with PC1 beyond B5 (held-out partial 0.120, $I^2 = 0$) but not with PC2 (partial $-$0.07 to $-$0.11).\n\n\\textbf{Sequence and closure tests.} A home-prominence half-peak vs off-home take-off test finds no signal beyond the mechanical lag (DEV excess $-$0.009 [$-$0.015, $-$0.003], held-out +0.011 [0.005, 0.016]). Intersection-born concepts take off later (HR 0.47 [0.42, 0.54]). A within-concept closure test\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-15}} is null on the development set (density PPML $b = -0.070$ [$-$0.180, 0.040]; OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ $b = +0.015$ [$-$0.038, 0.069]). On held-out fields, OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is opposite-signed ($-$0.079 [$-$0.146, $-$0.013]). Early openness is a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_entry_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient $d_0$ (log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) from the conditional-logit entry model (rung R3, controlling for home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density $D_{\\mathrm{rca}}$ and volume density $D_{\\mathrm{vol}}$), by unit. Circles with bars show point estimates with 95\\% concept-bootstrap confidence intervals. The light-blue row is the development (DEV) set used for selection. Dark-blue rows are the held-out domain groups and the 2010--14 onset cohort. The black diamond is the DerSimonian--Laird random-effects estimate pooled over the four held-out groups, and its width spans its 95\\% CI. The right column prints each estimate and interval; $n$ is the number of concepts in each unit. The dashed line marks $d_0 = 0$. $d_0$ is positive with a CI excluding zero in all three evaluable held-out groups (Physical Sciences 0.148, Life \\& Env.\\ 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297) and in the cohort (0.321). Math \\& Decision ($n = 165$, excluded as underpowered before the freeze) is null (0.065 [$-$0.110, 0.234]). The pooled estimate is 0.243 [0.118, 0.368] with high heterogeneity ($I^2 = 0.92$). The frozen verdict is nonetheless PARTIAL: the pre-registered volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.}\n  \\label{fig:entry}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{Discussion of RQ2}\n\nThe retained-frontier result extends the principle of relatedness to concept adoption. The positive coefficient is large and consistent across three of three evaluable groups, but the PARTIAL verdict limits its interpretation: we cannot fully separate persistence from sustained volume as a predictor of field entry. The effect is also backbone-specific: it holds on the sparse PMI backbone but not under the standard Hidalgo proximity. The breadth decomposition shows that integrating and localised concepts differ primarily in how many fields they contact early, not in how many more fields they enter later. The null closure test and opposite-signed held-out result indicate that openness does not operate as a within-concept mechanism driving diffusion.\n\n\n\\subsection{Confound analysis}\n\\label{sec:confound}\n\nThe openness signal could be an artefact of small yearly samples or of dynamic churn. We tested four null models\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-16}}:\n\n\\textbf{Fixed-size rarefaction.} Subsampling to 10 home papers per year retains 68\\% of the pooled association. The bias-corrected Chao estimator retains 91\\%.\n\n\\textbf{Within-concept permutation null.} The excess churn over a 200-draw within-concept year-label permutation null is indistinguishable from zero: excess NOVCHURN pooled PSP = +0.008 [$-$0.02, +0.03], compared to raw NOVCHURN = +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]. The $R^2$ of raw persistence on the permutation-null mean is 0.66. What predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix.\n\n\\textbf{Degree-preserving configuration null.} Replacing raw ego density and persistence by curveball configuration $z$-scores raises OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ from +0.092 to +0.115.\n\n\\textbf{Reliability.} Split-half reliability of NOVCHURN$_{\\text{raw}}$ is 0.48. The temporal-excess variants (V2) have split-half Spearman--Brown reliability of approximately 0.01--0.05, and the planted-churn check fails. The disattenuated pooled NOVCHURN PSP is 0.178 [0.141, 0.214] (approximate, CI not independently re-derived).\n\nBecause the V2 temporal-excess measure is unreliable, the analysis cannot adjudicate temporal churn at typical sample sizes ($\\sim$10 home papers/year). The association that survives behaves like a static dispersion property. Temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.\n\n\\textbf{Partner decomposition.} The home-only signal is carried by partners from new Leiden communities arriving through mixed-field papers: contrast $C_2$ = +0.102 [+0.069, +0.133] (Holm $p$ = 0.0025), domain Shapley $\\phi$ = +0.132 on the cohort (method = +0.012). Controlling for the share of early bridging papers halves NOVCHURN from 0.118 to 0.056.\n\n\n\\subsection{Exploratory AI-domain stage}\n\nAn exploratory retrospective atlas of 37 AI and computer science concepts was constructed from the large panel, examining how concepts such as deep learning, reinforcement learning and generative adversarial networks evolved through the co-occurrence network before their cross-field diffusion. This atlas is outcome-selected and retrospective; it provides qualitative context but no hypothesis-testing power.\n\n\n\\subsection{Representative case studies}\n\nSeven matched case-study pairs were drawn from the breadth decomposition analysis (Table~\\ref{tab:cases}; one pair is shown in Figure~\\ref{fig:case_study}). These pairs are illustration only; all are descriptive with no $p$-value.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Representative matched case-study pairs, contrasting high-breadth and low-breadth concepts matched on early volume. All pairs are illustration; no inferential claim is made.}\n\\label{tab:cases}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nHigh-breadth concept & Low-breadth concept & Group \\\\\n\\midrule\nGraphics processing unit & Vertical-axis wind turbine & Eng \\\\\nShotgun proteomics & Image-guided radiation therapy & BGM \\\\\nNanocarriers & Nanosheet & CS \\\\\nSoft power & Autonomous learning & SOC \\\\\nScopus & Oxygen reduction reaction & CS \\\\\nSclerostin & IgG4-related disease & BGM \\\\\nUser-generated content & Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy & SOC \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_case_study_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Illustrative matched case-study pair (pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset $t_0=2008$, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; $t_0=2009$, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from $t_0$ to $t_0+8$; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. (b,~c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years ($t_0$ to $t_0+2$, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field. GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30). VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness--breadth association and is not evidence for it.}\n  \\label{fig:case_study}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\n\\subsection{Dead ends and negative results}\n\\label{sec:dead_ends}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:deadends} lists the principal hypotheses and candidate signals that were tested and did not survive.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Principal dead ends and negative results.}\n\\label{tab:deadends}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}p{2.5cm}p{5.5cm}}\n\\toprule\nHypothesis / candidate & Decisive test & Result \\\\\n\\midrule\nNaturalisation gap ($A^*_h$) & Indicator screen & Fails every clause ($-$0.006) \\\\\n$D_{\\text{ratio}}$, $F_{\\text{res}}$ & Ratio indicators & No candidate survives \\\\\nGateway landing on $O_{2r}$ & Gateway analysis & $\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001 held-out \\\\\nH3 gateway-weighted landing & Gateway analysis & Pooled CI includes 0 [$-$0.006, 0.065] \\\\\nOrdering (central-first) & Trajectory analysis & MIXED: 32.6\\% of broad concepts; negative lead-lag; pre-trend \\\\\nTwo discrete trajectory classes & Trajectory clustering & HMM-vs-DTW ARI 0.094/0.222 \\\\\nAbandonment penalty ($d_{\\text{lost}}$) & Entry model & Specification-dependent: A1 $-$0.007, R4 +0.064, min-cp $-$0.030 \\\\\nVolume-matched retained-frontier contrast & Entry model & Null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] held-out \\\\\n$O_5$ external recognition & Indicator screen & No indicator beats B5 + onset year \\\\\nRescue and relay models & Trajectory analysis & Not supported \\\\\nWithin-concept closure & Closure test & Null on DEV; opposite-signed held-out ($-$0.079) \\\\\n$n_{\\text{authors\\_early}}$ for $O_3$ & Cohort replication & Non-replication on fresh cohort (+0.014) \\\\\nRETENTION\\_RATIO at R2/R3 & Cohort replication & Null on cohort ($-$0.043 [$-$0.116, 0.031]) \\\\\nTrait prediction ($P$-B1) & Reliability test & Fails: yearly OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ ICC 0.34--0.39 \\\\\nVocab-free Cheng reversal & Vocab-free frame & Not confirmed ($-$0.064 [$-$0.159, 0.031]) \\\\\nCo-author candidate S & Indicator screen & Computed; not confirmed for any outcome \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{What the openness index captures}\n\nThe OPEN index captures the degree to which a concept's early neighbourhood acquires partners from diverse communities rather than reinforcing existing ones. The signal is not demonstrably temporal turnover but a static topical-dispersion property. A within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component, yet the association persists: concepts whose home-field co-occurrence partners span many communities tend to reach more fields later. This is consistent with \\citeauthor{March1991}'s (\\citeyear{March1991}) exploration--exploitation distinction at the concept level. However, the within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields, indicating that openness operates as a between-concept trait rather than as a within-concept causal mechanism.\n\nThe home-only signal (OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$) is marginal. The stronger OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ signal is partly mechanically coupled: early off-home papers that enter the ego network are a subset of the papers that determine the outcome. OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ controls for this coupling and remains significant.\n\n\\subsection{Reconciling consistency and breadth}\n\n\\citet{Cheng2023} found that ideational consistency predicts a concept becoming ``core.'' We replicate their result for volume (+53\\%/SD) but show that, net of volume, the same property predicts \\emph{narrower} cross-field reach. The reversal holds in all five field groups ($I^2 = 0$) and replicates on a fresh cohort. The features predictive of local consolidation and growth are distinct from, and partly opposed to, the features predictive of broad disciplinary spread.\n\n\\subsection{The retained-frontier claim}\n\nThe confirmed field-entry result ($d_0 = 0.322$ on the independent frame) extends the principle of relatedness from economic geography \\citep{Hidalgo2007,Boschma2015} to concept adoption. The result is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is backbone-specific (it reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity). What survives is a PMI-backbone relative-odds effect that cannot be separated from volume. The $I^2$ of 0.92 indicates substantial cross-domain heterogeneity, with Life \\& Environment showing the strongest signal and Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences null.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\textbf{Effect size.} The OPEN--breadth association is modest. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [$-$0.003, +0.008]).\n\n\\textbf{Measurement noise.} Split-half reliability of OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.\n\n\\textbf{Vocabulary bias.} The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. Frame~N is small (636 concepts) with pre-unseal power of 0.47.\n\n\\textbf{Coupling.} About half of the OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction (which uses off-home papers) and the breadth outcome. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is free of this coupling but marginal.\n\n\\textbf{Domain heterogeneity.} Life \\& Environment shows the weakest OPEN signal (PSP +0.042). The retained-field relatedness $I^2$ is 0.92.\n\n\\textbf{Not causal.} Early ego-network openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.\n\n\\textbf{Prior unsealing.} Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments in the same project, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks.\n\n\n\\section{Conclusions}\n\\label{sec:conclusions}\n\nWe screened 53 early temporal network indicators for predicting the cross-disciplinary breadth of new scientific concepts, using 12{,}499 concepts from the OpenAlex corpus with held-out validation and a fresh cohort confirmation. Seven indicators are confirmed, composing into the OPEN index that captures topical non-redundancy in a concept's early co-occurrence neighbourhood. The signal is a static between-concept trait; temporal turnover could not be tested at available sample sizes. Early openness predicts breadth; early consolidation predicts volume but not breadth. Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them, but the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: persistence and volume are confounded, and the effect is backbone-specific.\n\n\n\\section*{Declarations}\n\n\\subsection*{Availability of data and materials}\n\\begin{sloppypar}\nThe study uses the publicly available OpenAlex bulk snapshot (2026-09-23). Analysis code is available at\n\\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP};\nindividual experiment folders are linked in the paper's footnotes. Concept frames and indicator matrices are available from the corresponding author upon request.\n\\end{sloppypar}\n\n\\subsection*{Competing interests}\nThe authors declare no competing interests.\n\n\\subsection*{Funding}\nNot applicable.\n\n\\subsection*{Authors' contributions}\nAll authors contributed to the study design, analysis and manuscript preparation.\n\n\\subsection*{Acknowledgements}\nNot applicable.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 437, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 437}}

<main id="main">

<header id="overview">
<h1>Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth</h1>
<p class="subtitle">Evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts</p>
<p class="author">AI Inventor</p>

<p class="tldr">Which early signals predict whether a scientific concept will cross disciplinary boundaries? We tracked 12,499 concepts from the OpenAlex corpus and found that the diversity and novelty of a concept's early topic co-occurrence partners predict later cross-field breadth. Seven indicators survive held-out validation and compose into an openness index whose pooled partial correlation with breadth is +0.069 across six independent validation groups: small, but positive in every one.</p>

<div class="doc-links">

<!-- ============ CONTRIBUTIONS ============ -->
<section id="contributions">
<h2>Contributions</h2>

<div class="card">
<h3>Seven confirmed network indicators</h3>
<p>Of 53 early co-occurrence network indicators screened against a five-feature popularity baseline, seven survive held-out validation for predicting rarefied cross-field breadth. Two carry negative signs: concepts with higher early field retention or denser ego-networks spread less broadly.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>The OPEN openness index</h3>
<p>A six-component composite measuring a concept's early tendency to acquire diverse, community-spanning co-occurrence partners. Pooled across six non-selection bodies, its partial Spearman correlation with later breadth is +0.069 [+0.038, +0.100], I<sup>2</sup> = 0, all bodies positive.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Retained-frontier entry</h3>
<p>Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them (d<sub>0</sub> = +0.322 [+0.291, +0.355] on 11,841 concepts). The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, persistence and volume remain confounded, and the result is backbone-specific.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Consistency predicts growth, not breadth</h3>
<p>Cheng et al.'s (2023) ideational consistency predicts volume growth but narrower cross-field reach. This reversal holds in all five field groups and replicates on a fresh cohort.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<h3>Contact diversity drives the breadth gap</h3>
<p>Early contact diversity accounts for 73% of the breadth gap between broadly and narrowly spreading concepts. No discrete trajectory typology is stable; diffusion paths form a continuum along a breadth axis.</p>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ METHOD ============ -->
<section id="method">
<h2>Method</h2>

<figure>
<img src="figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg" alt="Study design flowchart from OpenAlex snapshot through concept identification, panel split, indicator computation, to screening and validation results for both research questions">
<figcaption>Overview of the study design, read left to right. The OpenAlex snapshot (blue; 476M works, 129.4M base works 1995&ndash;2022) is title-matched against 56,643 legacy concepts, and Aho-Corasick matching plus an LLM precision gate (teal) keeps 12,499 grounded concepts. The panel split (green) assigns these to a development set (DEV 4,771; CS, Eng, BGM, Med homes, onset 2003&ndash;2009), four held-out domain groups (3,372; PHYS, LIFEENV, SOC, MATHDEC) and a 2010&ndash;2014 onset cohort (4,356). A fresh 2015&ndash;2017 cohort (1,443; dashed box) comes from a separate scan. For each concept, 53 early indicators in six families (orange; A ego-network 27, E popularity 6, F disciplinary 3, FR frontier 7, G gateway 7, S co-author 3) are computed in the t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2 window. They are screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1, top right): 7 frozen indicators are confirmed on held-out, and the pooled partial Spearman of the OPEN index is +0.069. Separately (lower arrow, bypassing the indicators), a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent concept frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2, bottom right). It gives d<sub>0</sub> = 0.322 for retained-frontier relatedness, and the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL because persistence is confounded with volume.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="method-text">
<p>The study starts from the OpenAlex bulk snapshot: 476 million works, of which 129.4 million are base works published between 1995 and 2022. Concepts are identified by Aho-Corasick title matching of 56,643 legacy OpenAlex concepts (levels 2&ndash;5) plus Wikidata aliases, with stemmed verification. A per-concept LLM precision gate drops concepts with precision below 0.80, yielding 12,499 grounded concepts.</p>

<p>These are split into a development set (DEV, 4,771 concepts with homes in Computer Science, Engineering, Biochemistry/Genetics/Medicine and Medicine, onset 2003&ndash;2009), four held-out domain groups (3,372 concepts in Physical Sciences, Life &amp; Environment, Social Sciences and Math &amp; Decision Sciences), a 2010&ndash;2014 onset cohort (4,356), and a fresh 2015&ndash;2017 cohort (1,443) never used in any earlier step.</p>

<p>The primary outcome is rarefied field breadth (O<sub>2r</sub>, m = 50): the expected number of distinct venue fields among 50 randomly drawn papers from years t<sub>0</sub>+6 to t<sub>0</sub>+8, computed by exact hypergeometric rarefaction. This separates size-adjusted breadth from sheer volume.</p>

<p>For each concept, 53 early indicators across six families (ego-network topology, popularity, disciplinary spread, retained frontier, gateway centrality and co-author reach) are computed over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2). These are screened against a five-feature popularity baseline (B5: log early volume, publication growth, non-home share, Shannon entropy, field reach) using partial Spearman priority with 2,000 concept-level bootstrap resamples. Cross-body pooling uses the DerSimonian&ndash;Laird random-effects estimator with I<sup>2</sup> heterogeneity reporting.</p>

<p>Seven indicators survive. They compose into the OPEN index, a six-component measure of early co-occurrence openness: new edge rate, number of Leiden communities reached, participation coefficient, neighbourhood novelty residual (all positive-signed), and ego density and edge persistence (both negative-signed). The z-score constants are frozen from DEV data.</p>

<p>Separately, a conditional logit (Breslow partial likelihood) models which field a concept enters next, stratified by concept-year. It tests whether relatedness to fields currently retaining the concept predicts entry, beyond relatedness to the home field, field size, entered density, gateway centrality, and conventional density measures. A field is "retaining" a concept when it has published at least two grounded papers on the concept in each of the two most recent years.</p>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ RESULTS ============ -->
<section id="results">
<h2>Results</h2>

<div class="finding">
<h3>Indicator screen and the OPEN index</h3>
<div class="finding-num">+0.069 [+0.038, +0.100]</div>
<p>Pooled partial Spearman of OPEN<sub>home</sub> with rarefied cross-field breadth across six non-selection bodies. I<sup>2</sup> = 0, all six positive. A single descriptive estimate. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/evaluation-4">(code)</a></p>
<p>Of 53 screened indicators, seven survive held-out validation with Holm correction. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/experiment-8">(code)</a> The strongest confirmed indicator is end-of-window field density (M0_density_end, pooled partial Spearman +0.375). Two confirmed indicators carry negative signs: early retention ratio (&minus;0.114) and ego density (&minus;0.102), meaning concepts with higher early field retention or denser local networks spread less broadly.</p>
<p>The DEV estimate is +0.109 [+0.073, +0.144], 1.58 times the non-selection pool, showing expected shrinkage from selection. On the 2015&ndash;2017 fresh cohort (1,443 concepts, never used in selection), OPEN<sub>home</sub> gives partial Spearman +0.091 [+0.013, +0.171] at control rung R2. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-4/experiment-10">(code)</a></p>
<p>A within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year churn component (excess NOVCHURN pooled +0.008 [&minus;0.02, +0.03]), indicating that what predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix, not temporal turnover. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-16">(code)</a></p>
</div>

<div class="finding">
<h3>Retained-frontier entry</h3>
<div class="finding-num">d<sub>0</sub> = 0.322 [0.291, 0.355]</div>
<p>Retained-frontier coefficient from the conditional-logit entry model on the independent held-out frame: 11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events, 6,076 informative strata. Log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields currently retaining the concept. Likelihood-ratio test vs. the R2 model: 325.8, p &lt; 10<sup>&minus;70</sup>. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/experiment-7">(code)</a></p>
<p>Positive in three of three evaluable held-out groups: Physical Sciences 0.148, Life &amp; Environment 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297. Mathematics &amp; Decision Sciences (n = 165) is null: 0.065 [&minus;0.109, 0.239]. DerSimonian&ndash;Laird pooled d<sub>0</sub> = 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], I<sup>2</sup> = 0.92.</p>
<p>The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast (comparing entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell) is null: &minus;0.028 [&minus;0.105, +0.046]. Under minimum-conditional-probability proximity instead of PMI, d<sub>0</sub> = &minus;0.021. Persistence and volume remain confounded, and the result is backbone-specific.</p>
</div>

<div class="finding">
<h3>Consistency predicts growth, not breadth</h3>
<div class="finding-num">+53.5%/SD raw, +1.3% net of volume, &minus;0.069 with breadth</div>
<p>Rebuilding Cheng et al.'s (2023) ideational consistency on OpenAlex topic co-usage for 12,311 concepts reproduces their volume estimate: b = 0.428 (+53.5%/SD for next-year volume). Adding current volume removes almost all of it: +1.3% [+0.5%, +2.1%], a residual-to-raw ratio of 0.021. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-14">(code)</a></p>
<p>Net of B5, the partial Spearman of consistency with rarefied breadth is &minus;0.069 [&minus;0.093, &minus;0.047] on the pooled bodies (I<sup>2</sup> = 0, 5/5 groups negative), replicating on the 2015&ndash;2017 cohort (&minus;0.111 [&minus;0.197, &minus;0.030]). The consistency measure has Spearman +0.77 with edge persistence. A stable neighbourhood predicts growth but not breadth.</p>
</div>

<div class="finding">
<h3>Breadth decomposition</h3>
<div class="finding-num">77.9% early contact diversity (DEV), 63.3% held-out</div>
<p>On 3,188 DEV concepts, the breadth gap between the top and bottom O<sub>2r</sub> terciles decomposes as: early contact diversity 77.9%, retention 26.8%, frontier advance &minus;4.6%. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-4/experiment-12">(code)</a> On the held-out pool excluding Medicine, the contact share is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727]. Broadly spreading and narrowly spreading concepts differ primarily in how many fields they contact early, not in how many more fields they enter later.</p>
<p>No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule: DTW k-medoids and HMM-based clustering on state sequences give an adjusted Rand index of 0.222. PCA reveals a continuum, with PC1 (38.8% of variance) as a breadth axis. A within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out (&minus;0.079 [&minus;0.146, &minus;0.013]): openness operates as a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-15">(code)</a></p>
</div>

<div class="finding">
<h3>Vocabulary-free replication</h3>
<div class="finding-num">+0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] on 636 phrase-born concepts</div>
<p>To address survivorship bias in the legacy vocabulary, 636 vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts (2003&ndash;2015 onsets) were identified. <a class="code-ref" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-13">(code)</a> OPEN<sub>home</sub> gives partial Spearman +0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] at control rung R3 for O<sub>2r</sub> (m = 30). The verdict is partial: the most demanding rung's confidence interval includes zero (+0.086 [&minus;0.009, +0.190]).</p>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ LIMITATIONS ============ -->
<section id="limitations">
<h2>Limitations</h2>

<ul class="limitations-list">
<li><strong>Effect size.</strong> The OPEN&ndash;breadth association is modest. OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds no forecasting gain over the popularity baseline (+0.002 [&minus;0.003, +0.008] Spearman).</li>
<li><strong>Measurement noise.</strong> Split-half reliability of OPEN<sub>home</sub> is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.</li>
<li><strong>Vocabulary bias.</strong> The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. The vocabulary-free frame has only 636 concepts with pre-unseal power of 0.47.</li>
<li><strong>Coupling.</strong> About half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction (which uses off-home papers) and the breadth outcome. OPEN<sub>home</sub> is free of this coupling but marginal.</li>
<li><strong>Domain heterogeneity.</strong> Life &amp; Environment shows the weakest OPEN signal (partial Spearman +0.042 vs pooled +0.069). The retained-field relatedness I<sup>2</sup> is 0.92.</li>
<li><strong>Not causal.</strong> Early ego-network openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.</li>
<li><strong>Prior unsealing.</strong> Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments in the same project, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks, not fully independent confirmations.</li>
</ul>
</section>

<!-- ============ EXPERIMENT CODE ============ -->
<section id="code" aria-label="Experiment code">

Inventor</p>\n\n<p class=\"tldr\">Which early signals predict whether a scientific concept will cross disciplinary boundaries? We tracked 12,499 concepts from the OpenAlex corpus and found that the diversity and novelty of a concept's early topic co-occurrence partners predict later cross-field breadth. Seven indicators survive held-out validation and compose into an openness index whose pooled partial correlation with breadth is +0.069 across six independent validation groups: small, but positive in every one.</p>\n\n<div class=\"doc-links\">\n<a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/paper.pdf\">Read ============ CONTRIBUTIONS ============ -->\n<section id=\"contributions\">\n<h2>Contributions</h2>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Seven confirmed network indicators</h3>\n<p>Of 53 early co-occurrence network indicators screened against a five-feature popularity baseline, seven survive held-out validation for predicting rarefied cross-field breadth. Two carry negative signs: concepts with higher early field retention or denser ego-networks spread less broadly.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>The OPEN openness index</h3>\n<p>A six-component composite measuring a concept's early tendency to acquire diverse, community-spanning co-occurrence partners. Pooled across six non-selection bodies, its partial Spearman correlation with later breadth is +0.069 [+0.038, +0.100], I<sup>2</sup> = 0, all bodies positive.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Retained-frontier entry</h3>\n<p>Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them (d<sub>0</sub> = +0.322 [+0.291, +0.355] on 11,841 concepts). The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, persistence and volume remain confounded, and the result is backbone-specific.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Consistency predicts growth, not breadth</h3>\n<p>Cheng et al.'s (2023) ideational consistency predicts volume growth but narrower cross-field reach. This reversal holds in all five field groups and replicates on a fresh cohort.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"card\">\n<h3>Contact diversity drives the breadth gap</h3>\n<p>Early contact diversity accounts for 73% of the breadth gap between broadly and narrowly spreading concepts. No discrete trajectory typology is stable; diffusion paths form a continuum along a breadth axis.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ METHOD ============ -->\n<section id=\"method\">\n<h2>Method</h2>\n\n<figure>\n<img src=\"figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Study design flowchart from OpenAlex snapshot through concept identification, panel split, indicator computation, to screening and validation results for both research questions\">\n<figcaption>Overview of the study design, read left to right. The OpenAlex snapshot (blue; 476M works, 129.4M base works 1995&ndash;2022) is title-matched against 56,643 legacy concepts, and Aho-Corasick matching plus an LLM precision gate (teal) keeps 12,499 grounded concepts. The panel split (green) assigns these to a development set (DEV 4,771; CS, Eng, BGM, Med homes, onset 2003&ndash;2009), four held-out domain groups (3,372; PHYS, LIFEENV, SOC, MATHDEC) and a 2010&ndash;2014 onset cohort (4,356). A fresh 2015&ndash;2017 cohort (1,443; dashed box) comes from a separate scan. For each concept, 53 early indicators in six families (orange; A ego-network 27, E popularity 6, F disciplinary 3, FR frontier 7, G gateway 7, S co-author 3) are computed in the t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2 window. They are screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1, top right): 7 frozen indicators are confirmed on held-out, and the pooled partial Spearman of the OPEN index is +0.069. Separately (lower arrow, bypassing the indicators), a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent concept frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2, bottom right). It gives d<sub>0</sub> = 0.322 for retained-frontier relatedness, and the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL because persistence is confounded with volume.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n\n<div class=\"method-text\">\n<p>The study starts from the OpenAlex bulk snapshot: 476 million works, of which 129.4 million are base works published between 1995 and 2022. Concepts are identified by Aho-Corasick title matching of 56,643 legacy OpenAlex concepts (levels 2&ndash;5) plus Wikidata aliases, with stemmed verification. A per-concept LLM precision gate drops concepts with precision below 0.80, yielding 12,499 grounded concepts.</p>\n\n<p>These are split into a development set (DEV, 4,771 concepts with homes in Computer Science, Engineering, Biochemistry/Genetics/Medicine and Medicine, onset 2003&ndash;2009), four held-out domain groups (3,372 concepts in Physical Sciences, Life &amp; Environment, Social Sciences and Math &amp; Decision Sciences), a 2010&ndash;2014 onset cohort (4,356), and a fresh 2015&ndash;2017 cohort (1,443) never used in any earlier step.</p>\n\n<p>The primary outcome is rarefied field breadth (O<sub>2r</sub>, m = 50): the expected number of distinct venue fields among 50 randomly drawn papers from years t<sub>0</sub>+6 to t<sub>0</sub>+8, computed by exact hypergeometric rarefaction. This separates size-adjusted breadth from sheer volume.</p>\n\n<p>For each concept, 53 early indicators across six families (ego-network topology, popularity, disciplinary spread, retained frontier, gateway centrality and co-author reach) are computed over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2). These are screened against a five-feature popularity baseline (B5: log early volume, publication growth, non-home share, Shannon entropy, field reach) using partial Spearman priority with 2,000 concept-level bootstrap resamples. Cross-body pooling uses the DerSimonian&ndash;Laird random-effects estimator with I<sup>2</sup> heterogeneity reporting.</p>\n\n<p>Seven indicators survive. They compose into the OPEN index, a six-component measure of early co-occurrence openness: new edge rate, number of Leiden communities reached, participation coefficient, neighbourhood novelty residual (all positive-signed), and ego density and edge persistence (both negative-signed). The z-score constants are frozen from DEV data.</p>\n\n<p>Separately, a conditional logit (Breslow partial likelihood) models which field a concept enters next, stratified by concept-year. It tests whether relatedness to fields currently retaining the concept predicts entry, beyond relatedness to the home field, field size, entered density, gateway centrality, and conventional density measures. A field is \"retaining\" a concept when it has published at least two grounded papers on the concept in each of the two most recent years.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ RESULTS ============ -->\n<section id=\"results\">\n<h2>Results</h2>\n\n<div class=\"finding\">\n<h3>Indicator screen and the OPEN index</h3>\n<div class=\"finding-num\">+0.069 [+0.038, +0.100]</div>\n<p>Pooled partial Spearman of OPEN<sub>home</sub> with rarefied cross-field breadth across six non-selection bodies. I<sup>2</sup> = 0, all six positive. A single descriptive estimate. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/evaluation-4\">(code)</a></p>\n<p>Of 53 screened indicators, seven survive held-out validation with Holm correction. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/experiment-8\">(code)</a> The strongest confirmed indicator is end-of-window field density (M0_density_end, pooled partial Spearman +0.375). Two confirmed indicators carry negative signs: early retention ratio (&minus;0.114) and ego density (&minus;0.102), meaning concepts with higher early field retention or denser local networks spread less broadly.</p>\n<p>The DEV estimate is +0.109 [+0.073, +0.144], 1.58 times the non-selection pool, showing expected shrinkage from selection. On the 2015&ndash;2017 fresh cohort (1,443 concepts, never used in selection), OPEN<sub>home</sub> gives partial Spearman +0.091 [+0.013, +0.171] at control rung R2. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-4/experiment-10\">(code)</a></p>\n<p>A within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year churn component (excess NOVCHURN pooled +0.008 [&minus;0.02, +0.03]), indicating that what predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix, not temporal turnover. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-16\">(code)</a></p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"finding\">\n<h3>Retained-frontier entry</h3>\n<div class=\"finding-num\">d<sub>0</sub> = 0.322 [0.291, 0.355]</div>\n<p>Retained-frontier coefficient from the conditional-logit entry model on the independent held-out frame: 11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events, 6,076 informative strata. Log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields currently retaining the concept. Likelihood-ratio test vs. the R2 model: 325.8, p &lt; 10<sup>&minus;70</sup>. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/experiment-7\">(code)</a></p>\n<p>Positive in three of three evaluable held-out groups: Physical Sciences 0.148, Life &amp; Environment 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297. Mathematics &amp; Decision Sciences (n = 165) is null: 0.065 [&minus;0.109, 0.239]. DerSimonian&ndash;Laird pooled d<sub>0</sub> = 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], I<sup>2</sup> = 0.92.</p>\n<p>The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast (comparing entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell) is null: &minus;0.028 [&minus;0.105, +0.046]. Under minimum-conditional-probability proximity instead of PMI, d<sub>0</sub> = &minus;0.021. Persistence and volume remain confounded, and the result is backbone-specific.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"finding\">\n<h3>Consistency predicts growth, not breadth</h3>\n<div class=\"finding-num\">+53.5%/SD raw, +1.3% net of volume, &minus;0.069 with breadth</div>\n<p>Rebuilding Cheng et al.'s (2023) ideational consistency on OpenAlex topic co-usage for 12,311 concepts reproduces their volume estimate: b = 0.428 (+53.5%/SD for next-year volume). Adding current volume removes almost all of it: +1.3% [+0.5%, +2.1%], a residual-to-raw ratio of 0.021. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-14\">(code)</a></p>\n<p>Net of B5, the partial Spearman of consistency with rarefied breadth is &minus;0.069 [&minus;0.093, &minus;0.047] on the pooled bodies (I<sup>2</sup> = 0, 5/5 groups negative), replicating on the 2015&ndash;2017 cohort (&minus;0.111 [&minus;0.197, &minus;0.030]). The consistency measure has Spearman +0.77 with edge persistence. A stable neighbourhood predicts growth but not breadth.</p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"finding\">\n<h3>Breadth decomposition</h3>\n<div class=\"finding-num\">77.9% early contact diversity (DEV), 63.3% held-out</div>\n<p>On 3,188 DEV concepts, the breadth gap between the top and bottom O<sub>2r</sub> terciles decomposes as: early contact diversity 77.9%, retention 26.8%, frontier advance &minus;4.6%. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-4/experiment-12\">(code)</a> On the held-out pool excluding Medicine, the contact share is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727]. Broadly spreading and narrowly spreading concepts differ primarily in how many fields they contact early, not in how many more fields they enter later.</p>\n<p>No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule: DTW k-medoids and HMM-based clustering on state sequences give an adjusted Rand index of 0.222. PCA reveals a continuum, with PC1 (38.8% of variance) as a breadth axis. A within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out (&minus;0.079 [&minus;0.146, &minus;0.013]): openness operates as a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-15\">(code)</a></p>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"finding\">\n<h3>Vocabulary-free replication</h3>\n<div class=\"finding-num\">+0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] on 636 phrase-born concepts</div>\n<p>To address survivorship bias in the legacy vocabulary, 636 vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts (2003&ndash;2015 onsets) were identified. <a class=\"code-ref\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-5/experiment-13\">(code)</a> OPEN<sub>home</sub> gives partial Spearman +0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] at control rung R3 for O<sub>2r</sub> (m = 30). The verdict is partial: the most demanding rung's confidence interval includes zero (+0.086 [&minus;0.009, +0.190]).</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ FIGURES ============ -->\n<section id=\"figures\">\n<h2>Figures</h2>\n\n<div class=\"gallery-item\">\n<figure>\n<div class=\"fig-link\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"View full size: Study design overview\" data-caption=\"Overview of the study design, read left to right. The OpenAlex snapshot (blue; 476M works, 129.4M base works 1995-2022) is title-matched against 56,643 legacy concepts, and Aho-Corasick matching plus an LLM precision gate (teal) keeps 12,499 grounded concepts. The panel split (green) assigns these to a development set (DEV 4,771; CS, Eng, BGM, Med homes, onset 2003-2009), four held-out domain groups (3,372; PHYS, LIFEENV, SOC, MATHDEC) and a 2010-2014 onset cohort (4,356). A fresh 2015-2017 cohort (1,443; dashed box) comes from a separate scan. For each concept, 53 early indicators in six families (orange; A ego-network 27, E popularity 6, F disciplinary 3, FR frontier 7, G gateway 7, S co-author 3) are computed in the t0 to t0+2 window. They are screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1, top right): 7 frozen indicators are confirmed on held-out, and the pooled partial Spearman of the OPEN index is +0.069. Separately (lower arrow, bypassing the indicators), a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent concept frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2, bottom right). The dotted vertical line marks this pooled estimate and the dashed line marks zero. Values at right are estimate [95% CI]. The association is small and has the same sign in every body, but only the two cohort rows and the pool have CIs above zero individually. All non-selection bodies except the 2015&ndash;17 cohort had outcomes read in earlier analyses, so the pool is descriptive rather than confirmatory.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"gallery-item\">\n<figure>\n<div class=\"fig-link\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"View full size: Retained-frontier entry across domains\" data-caption=\"Retained-frontier coefficient d0 (log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) from the conditional-logit entry model (rung R3), by unit. The frozen verdict is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.\">\n<img src=\"figures/fig_entry_v0.png\" alt=\"Forest plot of retained-frontier coefficients across domain groups, showing positive d-zero estimates and a pooled value of 0.243\">\n</div>\n<figcaption><strong>Figure 3: Retained-frontier entry across domains.</strong> Retained-frontier coefficient d<sub>0</sub> (log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) from the conditional-logit entry model (rung R3, controlling for home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density D<sub>rca</sub> and volume density D<sub>vol</sub>), by unit. The right column prints each estimate and interval; <em>n</em> is the number of concepts in each unit. The dashed line marks d<sub>0</sub> = 0. d<sub>0</sub> is positive with a CI excluding zero in all three evaluable held-out groups (Physical Sciences 0.148, Life &amp; Env. 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297) and in the cohort (0.321). Math &amp; Decision (n = 165, excluded as underpowered before the freeze) is null (0.065 [&minus;0.110, 0.234]). The pooled estimate is 0.243 [0.118, 0.368] with high heterogeneity (I<sup>2</sup> = 0.92). The frozen verdict is nonetheless PARTIAL: the pre-registered volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.</figcaption>\n</figure>\n</div>\n\n<div class=\"gallery-item\">\n<figure>\n<div class=\"fig-link\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"button\" aria-label=\"View full size: Matched case-study pair comparing GPU and VAWT\" data-caption=\"Illustrative matched case-study pair (pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset t0=2008, high OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; t0=2009, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Off-home fields entered and retained over time. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks: GPU has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30), VAWT has 12 topics in 1 community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness-breadth association and is not evidence for it.\">\n<img src=\"figures/fig_case_study_v0.png\" alt=\"Three-panel comparison of GPU (high openness, 34 topics in 8 communities) and VAWT (low openness, 12 topics in 1 community) showing field entry trajectories and topic co-occurrence ego networks\">\n</div>\n<figcaption><strong>Figure 4: Matched case-study pair.</strong> Illustrative matched case-study pair from Experiment 12 (case pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset t<sub>0</sub>=2008, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; t<sub>0</sub>=2009, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+8; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. By t<sub>0</sub>+2 GPU had entered 7 off-home fields and VAWT 2; by t<sub>0</sub>+8 they had entered 11 and 6 and retained 8 and 4. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the 2010&ndash;14 topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field of its topics (plus the runner-up field when it has at least 0.6 times as many). GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30), led by Engineering &amp; Physics, Computer Science and Medicine communities. VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness&ndash;breadth association and is not evidence for it (case_pairs.json, pair 1).</figcaption>\n</figure>\n</div>\n\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ LIMITATIONS ============ -->\n<section id=\"limitations\">\n<h2>Limitations</h2>\n\n<ul class=\"limitations-list\">\n<li><strong>Effect size.</strong> The OPEN&ndash;breadth association is modest. OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds no forecasting gain over the popularity baseline (+0.002 [&minus;0.003, +0.008] Spearman).</li>\n<li><strong>Measurement noise.</strong> Split-half reliability of OPEN<sub>home</sub> is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.</li>\n<li><strong>Vocabulary bias.</strong> The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. The vocabulary-free frame has only 636 concepts with pre-unseal power of 0.47.</li>\n<li><strong>Coupling.</strong> About half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction (which uses off-home papers) and the breadth outcome. OPEN<sub>home</sub> is free of this coupling but marginal.</li>\n<li><strong>Domain heterogeneity.</strong> Life &amp; Environment shows the weakest OPEN signal (partial Spearman +0.042 vs pooled +0.069). The retained-field relatedness I<sup>2</sup> is 0.92.</li>\n<li><strong>Not causal.</strong> Early ego-network openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.</li>\n<li><strong>Prior unsealing.</strong> Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments in the same project, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks, not fully independent confirmations.</li>\n</ul>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ EXPERIMENT CODE ============ -->\n<section id=\"code\" aria-label=\"Experiment code\">\n<h2>All experiment code</h2>\n<ul class=\"code-list\">\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-1/experiment-1\">Does citing a concept 'as your own' predict its spread?</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-1/experiment-3\">Do diverse topic ties predict concept spread?</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-1/experiment-4\">Where a concept lands early vs how broadly it spreads</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-2/experiment-5\">Do hub fields keep new concepts? Held-out test</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-2/experiment-6\">Where new scientific concepts spread next</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-2/evaluation-1\">Does the gateway-field retention signal replicate?</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-2/dataset-2\">When research concepts were officially recognised</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-2/research-1\">How our results compare with related papers</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/evaluation-2\">Auditing the record before the paper</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_hy6I3YyVxPEP/round-3/research-2\">Is 'fields that keep it' new? Prior art and venue check</a></li>\n<li><a
